result.topic_en: A heavily corrected Latin draft, with German notes, of the theses for the public disputation of Riemann's dissertation. It lists contested points: his definition of a function of a complex variable (diss. p. 16), a theorem from the dissertation that contradicts Cauchy, and the determination of such a function without relying on an analytic expression.

items.english: From those propositions about which contrary opinions are held among not unknown authors enjoying fame (illustrious by reputation), we note the following:

items.quote:
Methodi [-quae-] ad determinandam functionem complexae quanti-
tatis variabilis {+adhiberi+} [-plerumque-] [-adhiberi-] adhibitae solent, eo omnes valent [-in eo conveniunt-]

items.english: The methods usually employed to determine a function of a complex variable all have in common that they start from an analytic expression, by means of which the value of the function is given for every determinate value of the argument.

Those who touched on this before us held views far from ours: that the notion we used for the definition was either not to be attributed to it at all (the illustrious Cauchy, cf. Comptes rendus) or did not belong to the definition.

items.english: We have assigned the extent of the conditions which are necessary to determine the function.
